entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ashutosh Kumar Mishra,G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A for the State and perused the material
brought on record.

2.  This bail application has been filed by the applicant-accused in Case Crime No.600 of 2023,
under Sections - 498A, 323, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Tappal, District- Aligarh with the prayer to enlarge the applicant-accused on bail.
3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Applicant is father-in-law of deceased.
The marriage of deceased with son of applicant has taken place about seven months prior to the incident.

Only general allegations of dowry demand and harassment of deceased have been levelled against all the accused persons,
Idreesh vs State Of U.P. on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152924132/
1 including the applicant.

entities.text: Idreesh vs State Of U.P. on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was submitted that in post-mortem report, cause of death has been shown throttling but there is absolutely no evidence that applicant was involved in causing any injury to the deceased.
In fact, the husband of deceased has admitted in his statement before the police that in fit of rage, he has throttled the deceased to death.

Referring the statement of sister of deceased, who is also married in the same family, it was submitted that even as per her statement,
while she was going to the room of deceased, it was co-accused Hamsar, who has met her. Statement of some independent witnesses including Mirza Zain, were also referred and it was submitted that there is no credible evidence to show the involvement of the applicant in the incident of causing death of deceased.

Lastly, it was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 16.11.2023,
having no criminal history, and that in case the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that deceased has suffered death due to throttling within a short period of her marriage and there are allegations that she was being harassed by applicant and co-accused persons on account of dowry.

After causing death of deceased,
accused persons were trying to burn her body.
It was also stated that even before the incident, a complaint was made to the police regarding harassment of deceased.

5. Considering submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusations, period of detention and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, a case for bail is made out.
6. The bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant - Idreesh involved in aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing each a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:
i. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii.
The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate any of the prosecution witness.
iii. The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Idreesh vs State Of U.P. on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152924132/
2 8.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the Court concerned shall be at liberty to cancel bail of applicant in accordance with law.
